text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty triggered -> PD-12345: synth-canary-auth-failure. Page fired to on-call @alex. Summary: Canary probes failing with 401 across eu/us regions. Link: https://pagerduty.com/PD-12345

alex: saw the page, looking. multiple probes started returning 401s around 03:07 UTC.

sam: I can see an automated key rotation job ran ~03:00 UTC (infra/keys service). It rotated the canary API key and pushed to vault, but looks like prober config didn't pick it up.

maria: ok — important: is this user-facing or just probes?

alex: likely probes only. No errors reported from production endpoints, only synthetic hit path. but I'm still triaging.

sam: quick repro: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx-old" https://canary.example.com/health
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 03:07:12 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "invalid_token",
  "message": "token expired or invalid"
}
```

alex: thanks. checking prober logs now. tail from prober-eu-02: 
```
[03:07:11] auth: token_lookup failed -> 401
[03:07:11] probe: request failed (401) url=/health region=eu instance=prober-eu-02
[03:07:12] retrying with cached token -> 401
```

maria: runbook says for auth-related synthetic failures: verify rotation job and update prober secret or rollback rotation. Which is fastest?

sam: fastest is to push the new token into prober config (the rotation already generated it). The problem is prober reads secret from vault path `secret/canary/token-v2` but the job wrote to `secret/canary/token-v3`. We can either update prober to read v3 or re-add v2.

alex: I'll do a temporary quick fix: update prober env to point at new path, then restart the prober daemon for the pool. If that fails, roll back rotation.

pagerduty: PD-12345 acknowledged by alex at 03:11 UTC.

alex: pushing config change to canary-prober-config -> set VAULT_PATH=secret/canary/token-v3. Doing a rolling restart of prober pool (eu/us) with 30s stagger.

deploy-bot: Triggered rollout: prober-pool-eu (3/3) -> in_progress

sam: heads up: make sure we don't cause simultaneous restarts across all regions, keep 1 instance up.

alex: aware. restarting one at a time.

deploy-bot: prober-pool-eu node1 updated -> success

alex: node1 restored, probes passing on node1 now. Watching for flapping.

deploy-bot: prober-pool-eu node2 updated -> success

alex: node2 good. node3 updating...

deploy-bot: prober-pool-eu node3 updated -> success. rollout complete for EU.

alex: EU pool green, probe pass rate 100% for test set. Starting US pool.

deploy-bot: prober-pool-us node1 updated -> success

alex: US pool now 80% passing, a few retries. Looks like one instance had stale env cached; forcing restart fixed it.

maria: good work. any customer impact?

sam: checked production metrics — no traffic errors, no increase in 5xx, no customer incidents reported. This is noisy-alert only.

maria: mark impact as "no customer-facing impact" in PD and link to runbook. Also update incident with root cause: rotation wrote to v3 path, probers still reading v2.

alex: updating PD notes and closing out. Quick postmortem action items:
- sam: make rotation job update the `prober_consumer` to alias latest token path or write back to v2 path for compatibility.
- devex: add alert suppression if probe auth fails for <10m across >1 region to avoid paging noise.
- infra: add health-check in rotation pipeline to validate downstream consumers.

sam: noted, will open ticket (INFRA-4521) and schedule a small fix.

pagerduty: PD-12345 -> resolved by alex at 03:27 UTC.

alex: handing off to maria for any follow-ups. I'll stay available for 15m.

maria: thanks. I'll own the postmortem and ensure runbook gets updated. Closing thread after runbook PR. :white_check_mark:
